diagnostics.message: The schedule aws_scheduler_schedule.pool targets role aws_iam_role.scheduler, but nothing orders aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler (which grants lambda:InvokeFunction) before the schedule. The schedule is enabled on creation and may fire before its execution role has any permissions, causing AccessDenied on the first invocations.

The function aws_lambda_function.pool only depends on the bare role aws_iam_role.pool; the inline policy aws_iam_role_policy.pool (SSM/KMS/GitHub-app parameter permissions) is created concurrently with the function. The function can therefore be invoked — e.g. by the EventBridge schedule created right after it — before its execution role is permissioned. The provider documentation recommends ordering the function after its role policies.

When aws_lambda_function.pool is configured with vpc_config, it needs ENI permissions from aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.pool_vpc_execution_role, but nothing orders that attachment before the function. The attachment is created concurrently with the function, so early invocations can fail until the AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole policy is attached. The aws_lambda_function documentation shows ordering the function after its role policy attachments.
